title: 2018 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: Triangle \(ABC\) with \(AB = 50\) and \(AC = 10\) has area \(120.\) Let \(D\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AB},\) and let \(E\) be the midpoint of \(\overline{AC}.\) The angle bisector of \(\angle BAC\) intersects \(\overline{DE}\) and \(\overline{BC}\) at \(F\) and \(G,\) respectively. What is the area of quadrilateral \(FDBG?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(D\) and \(E\) are midpoints, \(\triangle ADE\) has \(\tfrac14\) the area of \(\triangle ABC,\) namely \(30,\) so trapezoid \(EDBC\) has area \(120 - 30 = 90.\)

By the Angle Bisector Theorem, \(G\) divides \(BC\) with \(BG = \tfrac{AB}{AB + AC} \cdot BC = \tfrac56 BC,\) and likewise \(F\) divides \(DE\) so that \(DF = \tfrac56 DE.\) Because \(FDBG\) and \(EDBC\) share the same height, the area of \(FDBG\) is \(\tfrac56\) of the area of \(EDBC:\) \(\tfrac56 \cdot 90 = 75.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Since \(D, E\) are midpoints, \([ADE] = \tfrac14 [ABC],\) so trapezoid \(EDBC\) is the remaining \(\tfrac34\)
By the Angle Bisector Theorem the bisector cuts \(DE\) and \(BC\) in ratio \(AB : AC = 5 : 1,\) making \(FDBG\) equal to \(\tfrac56\) of \(EDBC\)
